title: Plot the standard normal curve with your own score scales — standard_normal_custom
code: standard_normal_custom()  # your own scales: tick marks for a test score and bands for performance levels my_scales<-rbind(data.frame(scale="SCORE",z=-3:3,z_end=NA,label=seq(20,80,10)),                  data.frame(scale="LEVEL",z=c(-4,-1,1),z_end=c(-1,1,4),label=c("Low","Average","High"))) standard_normal_custom(my_scales)  # start from the standard scales, drop the grades and add Wechsler scaled scores (mean 10, SD 3) scales<-standard_normal_scales_data() scales<-scales[scales$scale!="GRADE",] scales<-rbind(scales,data.frame(scale="SCALED",z=-3:3,z_end=NA,label=seq(1,19,3),colour=NA)) standard_normal_custom(scales)

title: Plot the standard normal curve with score scales — standard_normal_plot
text: scales placed z axis: z: standard score, mean 0 standard deviation 1. T: \(50 + 10z\). Percentile: z values 1st, 5th, 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 90th,     95th 99th percentiles. Sten: ten bands half standard deviation wide, sten 1 \(z = -2\)     sten 10 \(z = 2\) (mean 5.5, standard deviation 2). Stanine: nine bands half standard deviation wide, stanine 5     \(z = -0.25\) \(z = 0.25\) (mean 5, standard deviation 2). Grade: groups stanines, E (1-2), D (3), C (4-6), B (7) (8-9). IQ: \(100 + 15z\). coloured sten, stanine grade bands drawn thick lines, whose thickness follow size figure, figures ordinary size spill rows . standard_normal_scales draws chart fits figure size.
